source_read: Saved PubMed Central page text (PMC5027896, author manuscript), read in full: abstract, sections 1–6, Key points, disclosures and funding statement; reference list checked for the cited studies (99 entries). No tables or figures.

anchors.note: The same sentence says a sizable subgroup of first-episode presentations are children or adolescents, cited to ref 88, which by its title is a review of atypical antipsychotics in aggressive children and adolescents (card reporting issue 3); the paragraph adds that young people appear especially vulnerable to antipsychotic adverse effects (ref 89).

anchors.locator: 3.2 Duration (16% and 17%, refs 12 and 47; nearly 40% within 6 years, ref 57); 5.1, 1st paragraph, last sentence (remission within a week, no citation); reference list, refs 12 and 47 (editors' appraisal)
anchors.note: Factual basis confirmed: refs 12 (Chen et al., 2003) and 47 (Chen et al., 2005) share their first five authors (Chen, Lin, Sham, Ball, Loh); the 5.1 remission sentence carries no citation (3.2 cites refs 28, 30, 52 and 53 for recovery within a week); this review gives the Thai figure as nearly 40% within 6 years, and Wearne & Cornish (2018) give 38.8% at 5-year follow-up (The relationship between METH-induced psychosis and schizophrenia, 1st paragraph; ref 91), confirmed in that review's saved text.

for_senior_author: Risk of bias: re-appraised today by AI reader 3 with the editors' narrative-review checklist (overall high); reader 2's 'agree' was given to the superseded AMSTAR 2 rating. Domain judgments not re-judged here.

Interpretation gap: reader 2 agrees (substantial) and would add that 'efficacious' rests on two head-to-head trials without placebo arms while the same section reports remission within about a week of abstinence (now a note on key finding 10). Interpretation-gap text unchanged.
not_added: Section 5.1, 3rd paragraph describes medication practice for agitation (reader 2's third missed item): the card carries only that benzodiazepines may be used, with no administration detail; nothing to change.
Recurrence triggers that do not involve methamphetamine (heavy alcohol use, sleep deprivation, psychosocial stress): already in key finding 8; a matter for the wording of cl_meth_psychosis_course.
